item.title: Example Talk
item.description:
Click on the Slides button above to view the built-in slides feature.

Slides can be added in a few ways:

  • Create slides using Academic’s Slides feature and link using slides parameter in the front matter of the talk file
  • Upload an existing slide deck to static/ and link using url_slides parameter in the front matter of the talk file
  • Embed your slides (e.g. Google Slides) or presentation video on this page using shortcodes.

Further talk details can easily be added to this page using Markdown and $\rm \LaTeX$ math code.

<section aria-labelledby="space-weather-title" class="space-fold-section" id="space-weather"><details class="space-fold space-main-fold"><summary class="space-fold-heading"><h2 class="space-section space-fold-title" id="space-weather-title">Weather in Hong Kong</h2></summary><div class="space-fold-content">
<p>November is generally mild and relatively dry in Hong Kong. Based on the Hong Kong Observatory’s 1991–2020 climate normals, the <strong>average daily high is 24.5°C (76°F)</strong> and the <strong>average daily low is 20.3°C (69°F)</strong>. Average November rainfall is <strong>39.3 mm (1.5 in)</strong>, with <strong>5.7 days of measurable rain</strong>.</p>
<p class="space-small">See the <a href="https://www.hko.gov.hk/en/cis/normal/1991_2020/normals.htm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Hong Kong Observatory’s historical climate normals ↗</a> and <a href="https://www.hko.gov.hk/en/wxinfo/currwx/fnd.htm" target="_blank" rel="noopener">9-day weather forecast ↗</a>.</p>

    document.querySelectorAll('.space26 a[href^="#"]').forEach(function (a) {
      a.addEventListener('click', function () { revealSpaceTarget(decodeURIComponent(a.getAttribute('href').slice(1))); });
    });
    revealSpaceTarget(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)));
    var navLinks = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.space26 .space-localnav a[href^="#"]'));
    function updateNav(target) {
      navLinks.forEach(function (link) {
        if (link.getAttribute('href') === '#' + target) link.setAttribute('aria-current', 'location');
        else link.removeAttribute('aria-current');
      });
    }
    navLinks.forEach(function (link) {
      link.addEventListener('click', function () { updateNav(link.getAttribute('href').slice(1)); });
    });
    if (location.hash) updateNav(decodeURIComponent(location.hash.slice(1)));
  }

  else startSpaceFolds();

(function () {
  function initTaxiAudio() {
    document.querySelectorAll('.space26 .space-taxi-speak').forEach(function (button) {
      var panel = button.closest('.space-taxi-instructions');
      var status = panel && panel.querySelector('.space-taxi-speech-status');
      var label = button.querySelector('span');
      if (!panel || !status || !label) return;
      if (!('speechSynthesis' in window) || !('SpeechSynthesisUtterance' in window)) {
        button.disabled = true;
        status.textContent = 'Voice playback is unavailable in this browser; please show the address above.';
        return;
      }
      var synth = window.speechSynthesis;
      function reset() { label.textContent = 'Play Cantonese'; button.removeAttribute('aria-pressed'); }
      function cantoneseVoice() {
        var voices = synth.getVoices();
        return voices.find(function (v) { return /^yue(?:[-_]|$)/i.test(v.lang); }) ||
          voices.find(function (v) { return /^zh[-_]HK(?:[-_]|$)/i.test(v.lang); }) ||
          voices.find(function (v) { return /cantonese|廣東話|粵語|粤语/i.test(v.name); });
      }
      button.addEventListener('click', function () {
        if (synth.speaking || synth.pending) synth.cancel();
        var voice = cantoneseVoice();
        var voiceList = synth.getVoices();
        if (!voice && voiceList.length) {
          reset();
          status.textContent = 'No Cantonese voice is available on this device. Please show the written address to the driver.';
          return;
        }
        // Cantonese-only playback; the on-screen address retains IAS building details.
        var utterance = new SpeechSynthesisUtterance('唔該，去香港科技大學嘅賽馬會高等研究院，西貢清水灣道。');
        utterance.lang = voice ? voice.lang : 'zh-HK';
        if (voice) utterance.voice = voice;
        utterance.rate = .88;
        utterance.onstart = function () {
          label.textContent = 'Playing…'; button.setAttribute('aria-pressed','true');
          status.textContent = voice ? '' : 'Using the device voice; Cantonese pronunciation may vary.';
        };
        utterance.onend = reset;
        utterance.onerror = function () {
          synth.cancel();
          reset();
          status.textContent = 'Playback failed. Please show the written address to the driver.';
        };
        try { synth.speak(utterance); }
        catch (err) { synth.cancel(); reset(); status.textContent = 'Playback unavailable. Please show the written address to the driver.'; }
      });
    });
  }
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', initTaxiAudio);
  else initTaxiAudio();
})();

Writing technical content in Academic
item.description:
Academic is designed to give technical content creators a seamless experience. You can focus on the content and Academic handles the rest.

Highlight your code snippets, take notes on math classes, and draw diagrams from textual representation.

On this page, you’ll find some examples of the types of technical content that can be rendered with Academic.

Examples

Code

Academic supports a Markdown extension for highlighting code syntax. You can enable this feature by toggling the highlight option in your config/_default/params.toml file.

```python
import pandas as pd
data = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
data.head()
```

renders as

import pandas as pd
data = pd.read_csv("data.csv")
data.head()

Math

Academic supports a Markdown extension for $\LaTeX$ math. You can enable this feature by toggling the math option in your config/_default/params.toml file.

To render inline or block math, wrap your LaTeX math with $...$ or $$...$$, respectively.

Example math block:

$$\gamma_{n} = \frac{ 
\left | \left (\mathbf x_{n} - \mathbf x_{n-1} \right )^T 
\left [\nabla F (\mathbf x_{n}) - \nabla F (\mathbf x_{n-1}) \right ] \right |}
{\left \|\nabla F(\mathbf{x}_{n}) - \nabla F(\mathbf{x}_{n-1}) \right \|^2}$$

renders as

$$\gamma_{n} = \frac{ \left | \left (\mathbf x_{n} - \mathbf x_{n-1} \right )^T \left [\nabla F (\mathbf x_{n}) - \nabla F (\mathbf x_{n-1}) \right ] \right |}{\left |\nabla F(\mathbf{x}{n}) - \nabla F(\mathbf{x}{n-1}) \right |^2}$$

Example inline math $\nabla F(\mathbf{x}_{n})$ renders as $\nabla F(\mathbf{x}_{n})$.

Example multi-line math using the \\\\ math linebreak:

$$f(k;p_0^*) = \begin{cases} p_0^* & \text{if }k=1, \\\\
1-p_0^* & \text {if }k=0.\end{cases}$$

renders as

$$f(k;p_0^) = \begin{cases} p_0^ & \text{if }k=1, \\ 1-p_0^* & \text {if }k=0.\end{cases}$$

Diagrams

Academic supports a Markdown extension for diagrams. You can enable this feature by toggling the diagram option in your config/_default/params.toml file or by adding diagram: true to your page front matter.

An example flowchart:

```mermaid
graph TD
A[Hard] -->|Text| B(Round)
B --> C{Decision}
C -->|One| D[Result 1]
C -->|Two| E[Result 2]
```

renders as

graph TD
A[Hard] -->|Text| B(Round)
B --> C{Decision}
C -->|One| D[Result 1]
C -->|Two| E[Result 2]

An example sequence diagram:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
Alice->>John: Hello John, how are you?
loop Healthcheck
    John->>John: Fight against hypochondria
end
Note right of John: Rational thoughts!
John-->>Alice: Great!
John->>Bob: How about you?
Bob-->>John: Jolly good!
```

renders as

sequenceDiagram
Alice->>John: Hello John, how are you?
loop Healthcheck
    John->>John: Fight against hypochondria
end
Note right of John: Rational thoughts!
John-->>Alice: Great!
John->>Bob: How about you?
Bob-->>John: Jolly good!

An example Gantt diagram:

```mermaid
gantt
section Section
Completed :done,    des1, 2014-01-06,2014-01-08
Active        :active,  des2, 2014-01-07, 3d
Parallel 1   :         des3, after des1, 1d
Parallel 2   :         des4, after des1, 1d
Parallel 3   :         des5, after des3, 1d
Parallel 4   :         des6, after des4, 1d
```

renders as

gantt
section Section
Completed :done,    des1, 2014-01-06,2014-01-08
Active        :active,  des2, 2014-01-07, 3d
Parallel 1   :         des3, after des1, 1d
Parallel 2   :         des4, after des1, 1d
Parallel 3   :         des5, after des3, 1d
Parallel 4   :         des6, after des4, 1d

An example class diagram:

```mermaid
classDiagram
Class01 <|-- AveryLongClass : Cool
<<interface>> Class01
Class09 --> C2 : Where am i?
Class09 --* C3
Class09 --|> Class07
Class07 : equals()
Class07 : Object[] elementData
Class01 : size()
Class01 : int chimp
Class01 : int gorilla
class Class10 {
  <<service>>
  int id
  size()
}
```

renders as

classDiagram
Class01 <|-- AveryLongClass : Cool
<<interface>> Class01
Class09 --> C2 : Where am i?
Class09 --* C3
Class09 --|> Class07
Class07 : equals()
Class07 : Object[] elementData
Class01 : size()
Class01 : int chimp
Class01 : int gorilla
class Class10 {
  <<service>>
  int id
  size()
}

An example state diagram:

```mermaid
stateDiagram
[*] --> Still
Still --> [*]
Still --> Moving
Moving --> Still
Moving --> Crash
Crash --> [*]
```

renders as

stateDiagram
[*] --> Still
Still --> [*]
Still --> Moving
Moving --> Still
Moving --> Crash
Crash --> [*]

Todo lists

You can even write your todo lists in Academic too:

- [x] Write math example
- [x] Write diagram example
- [ ] Do something else

renders as

  • Write math example
  • Write diagram example
  • Do something else

Tables

Represent your data in tables:

| First Header  | Second Header |
| ------------- | ------------- |
| Content Cell  | Content Cell  |
| Content Cell  | Content Cell  |

renders as

First Header Second Header
Content Cell Content Cell
Content Cell Content Cell

Asides

Academic supports a shortcode for asides, also referred to as notices, hints, or alerts. By wrapping a paragraph in {{% alert note %}} ... {{% /alert %}}, it will render as an aside.

{{% alert note %}}
A Markdown aside is useful for displaying notices, hints, or definitions to your readers.
{{% /alert %}}

renders as

A Markdown aside is useful for displaying notices, hints, or definitions to your readers.

Spoilers

Add a spoiler to a page to reveal text, such as an answer to a question, after a button is clicked.

{{< spoiler text="Click to view the spoiler" >}}
You found me!
{{< /spoiler >}}

renders as

Click to view the spoiler

You found me!

Icons

Academic enables you to use a wide range of icons from Font Awesome and Academicons in addition to emojis.

Here are some examples using the icon shortcode to render icons:

{{< icon name="terminal" pack="fas" >}} Terminal  
{{< icon name="python" pack="fab" >}} Python  
{{< icon name="r-project" pack="fab" >}} R

renders as

Welcome to Academic!

Install Python and JupyterLab

Install Anaconda which includes Python 3 and JupyterLab.

Alternatively, install JupyterLab with pip3 install jupyterlab.

Create or upload a Jupyter notebook

Run the following commands in your Terminal, substituting <MY-WEBSITE-FOLDER> and <SHORT-POST-TITLE> with the file path to your Academic website folder and a short title for your blog post (use hyphens instead of spaces), respectively:

mkdir -p <MY-WEBSITE-FOLDER>/content/post/<SHORT-POST-TITLE>/
cd <MY-WEBSITE-FOLDER>/content/post/<SHORT-POST-TITLE>/
jupyter lab index.ipynb

The jupyter command above will launch the JupyterLab editor, allowing us to add Academic metadata and write the content.

Edit your post metadata

The first cell of your Jupter notebook will contain your post metadata ( front matter).

In Jupter, choose Markdown as the type of the first cell and wrap your Academic metadata in three dashes, indicating that it is YAML front matter:

---
title: My post's title
date: 2019-09-01

# Put any other Academic metadata here...
---

Edit the metadata of your post, using the documentation as a guide to the available options.

To set a featured image, place an image named featured into your post’s folder.

For other tips, such as using math, see the guide on writing content with Academic.

Convert notebook to Markdown

jupyter nbconvert index.ipynb --to markdown --NbConvertApp.output_files_dir=.

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com.

You can embed an R code chunk like this:

summary(cars)
##      speed           dist       
##  Min.   : 4.0   Min.   :  2.00  
##  1st Qu.:12.0   1st Qu.: 26.00  
##  Median :15.0   Median : 36.00

##  3rd Qu.:19.0   3rd Qu.: 56.00  
##  Max.   :25.0   Max.   :120.00
fit <- lm(dist ~ speed, data = cars)
fit
## 
## Call:
## lm(formula = dist ~ speed, data = cars)
## 
## Coefficients:
## (Intercept)        speed  
##     -17.579        3.932

Including Plots

You can also embed plots. See Figure 1 for example:

par(mar = c(0, 1, 0, 1))

  c(280, 60, 20),
  c('Sky', 'Sunny side of pyramid', 'Shady side of pyramid'),
  col = c('#0292D8', '#F7EA39', '#C4B632'),
